title: Balanced Partition Minimum Difference
statement:
You are given an array of `n` non-negative integers. Divide the array into two parts so that every element belongs to exactly one part, the numbers of elements in the two parts differ by **at most 1**, and the absolute difference between the sums of the two parts is as small as possible.

The parts are arbitrary subsets of the elements, not necessarily contiguous pieces of the array. When `n = 1`, one part holds the single element and the other part is empty.

Print the minimum possible absolute difference between the two sums.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` space-separated integers, the elements of the array.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the minimum possible absolute difference of the two part sums.

examples.explanation: Each part must have exactly 2 elements. `{1, 4}` and `{2, 3}` both sum to 5, so the difference is 0.
The parts have sizes 2 and 3. Taking `{10, 25}` (sum 35) leaves `{20, 15, 5}` (sum 40), a difference of 5. No split of sizes 2 and 3 gets closer to the half-sum 37.5.
One part contains 7 and the other is empty.

complexity.time: O(n² · S) where S is the sum of the array (O(n² · S / 64) with bitsets)

hints: The sizes are forced: one part has floor(n / 2) elements and the other has the rest. So you only need to know which sums are reachable by choosing exactly floor(n / 2) elements.
Track reachable (number of chosen elements, sum) pairs with a DP over the elements. Process the counts downwards so each element is used at most once.
For each count keep the set of reachable sums as a bitset (a big integer): adding element x is a shift by x. Finally pick the reachable sum s that minimizes |S - 2s|.
